correctness.rationale: The exact Hankel matrix is \(\begin{psmallmatrix}\bar a&\bar b\\\bar b&0\end{psmallmatrix}\). Its norm, the normalized-kernel profile, strict concavity, and the symbolic identity \((1-\tau/4)(1+\tau^2/4)-25/27=(8-3\tau)(3\tau-2)^2/432\) prove the bound for \(0<\tau\le1\). At \(\tau=2/3\), the test radius is the unique critical point. Complex phases and monomial boundary cases are handled. The 9,853 supplemental finite tests do not replace this universal proof.

value.rationale: The recent primary paper singles out \(az+z^2\) as a strict testing failure in a general open problem. The exact optimal norm-comparison constant across every quadratic symbol and all equality cases determine a natural, non-implied benchmark for kernel testing. It quantifies a structurally natural two-dimensional Hankel family, rather than a cherry-picked coefficient value, and distinguishes sharp inequalities from qualitative equality classifications.
